items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Frank Williams’ trumpet was the lightest trumpet I ever held. I always liked it, and he says, “You could play it if you want to.”

ctx.x: Yeah. I thought about it a lot, surprisingly a lot. I scoped out what I wanted to do pretty quickly and stuck to it very seriously. I mean for a minute there I wanted to be a trumpet player. I got a trumpet and I practiced too much, as my neighbors I’m sure could tell you, and I got a little bit of facility in the upper register, but I played stupid. And I was smart enough to know I was playing stupid. When I played with rock & roll bands, you know, I just recently ran into this guy, he actually had a minor…

and I’m sure I was attracted to a couple of young females who I went to high school with down there. But I was playing with the rhythm & blues, or soul as it was starting to be called, upstairs. And the sound was good. And I used to talk to the sound guy. And then I’d go hear Roy Eldridge, that was say a Saturday night dance on Sunday I’d say, “Roy, you know the sound isn’t too good.” He said “I’m hip, tell me about it, please believe me I need help.” And gradually I became an audio guy. And this really, I think,…
Right. Well you got into the radio through Columbia University.
